answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by slowly accumulating escrowed stake from completed, fee-paying tasks; newly created identities therefore begin with no influence, and splitting one agent into many does not multiply the stake. A nebula of accounts still faces the same capital requirement: an attacker must buy or borrow real stake, lock it for the vesting period, and risk losing it to slashing for provable fraud. The inlet is open, but the prism of escrow and penalties makes fake identities costly rather than free.
